Context/Background: To find novel treatments and drug combinations that could effectively target colorectal cancer cells (CRCs) and lower the probability of disease relapse, we designed multiple different combinations between cisplatin, cannabidiol (CBD), and intermittent serum starvation (ISS) on colorectal cancer cell lines. We analyzed differentially expressed genes and affected pathways in colorectal cancer cell lines to understand further the potential molecular mechanisms behind the treatments and their interactions.
Prompt: Based on the results of the differential expression analysis of ISS vs DMSO in colorectal cancer cells, run a pathway overrepresentation analysis for statistically significant genes (up and down combined) against the Reactome database. Then, provide a discussion of any relevant affected pathways, highlighting important up and down regulated genes in each.  Focus on any mechanisms by which intermittent serum starvation may alter cancer related pathways.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
The dataset derives from RNA-seq differential expression (DE) analysis comparing intermittent serum starvation (ISS) versus DMSO control in colorectal cancer (CRC) cell lines (Contrast “serum_starv_vs_dmso”). DESeq2 identified 6 555 significant genes (padj < 0.05). An Over-Representation Analysis (ORA) against Reactome pathways was performed on this combined list of up- and down-regulated genes to uncover affected molecular processes by ISS in CRC cells.

Keywords  
• Cholesterol biosynthesis  
• SREBP regulation  
• Membrane trafficking  
• p53–cell-cycle arrest  
• Peroxisomal protein processing  

Candidate Genes  
HMGCR, SREBF1, CYP51A1, TP53, CDC25C, PLK3, FASN  

Pathway Enrichments (Reactome ORA on combined sig. genes)  
| Term                                                     | Overlap | Adj P-value       | Leading Genes (excerpt)                           |  
|----------------------------------------------------------|---------|-------------------|---------------------------------------------------|  
| Membrane Trafficking                                     | 302 / 633 | 4.27 × 10⁻¹⁵      | ITSN2; TFRC; AKT1; ARF1; COPA; RAB1A; SEC23A; …    |  
| Intra-Golgi and Retrograde Golgi-to-ER Traffic           | 109 / 204 | 9.92 × 10⁻⁹       | KDELR1; GOLGA4; COPA; ARFGAP1; DYNC1H1; TUBB4A; …   |  
| Regulation of Cholesterol Biosynthesis by SREBP (SREBF)  | 42 / 56   | 6.70 × 10⁻⁹       | IDI1; MVK; INSIG1; HMGCR; SREBF1; FDPS; SCAP; …     |  
| Cholesterol Biosynthesis                                 | 23 / 27   | 1.37 × 10⁻⁶       | IDI1; FDPS; SREBF1; MVK; HMGCS1; CYP51A1; SQLE; …   |  
| TP53 Regulates Transcription of G2 Cell Cycle Arrest     | 17 / 21   | 1.93 × 10⁻⁴       | PLK3; BTG2; GADD45A; CDC25C; SFN; TP53; E2F4; …     |  

Balanced Analysis  
ISS in CRC cells drives a strong signature of lipid-metabolism rewiring: multiple tiers of the SREBP-mediated cholesterol synthesis program (SREBF regulation, core cholesterol biosynthesis) are enriched (42/56 and 23/27 genes; adj P < 10⁻⁶), including upregulation of HMGCR, SREBF1, CYP51A1 and FASN. This likely reflects a compensatory response to nutrient deprivation to maintain membrane integrity and signaling lipids. Concurrently, core membrane-trafficking pathways (anterograde and retrograde ER-Golgi transport; 302/633 genes) are overrepresented, suggesting altered secretory flux under serum withdrawal. A p53-driven G2 arrest program is also enriched (17/21 genes; adj P = 1.93 × 10⁻⁴), underscored by CDC25C, PLK3, SFN and TP53 itself, pointing to cell-cycle checkpoint activation. Together, these results imply that ISS triggers both adaptive metabolism (lipogenesis) and stress-induced cell-cycle control.

Key Genes/Proteins (leading edge)  
| Gene   | Direction* | Role/Function                       | Pathway(s)                                   |  
|--------|------------|-------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|  
| HMGCR  | Up         | Rate-limiting HMG-CoA reductase      | Cholesterol biosynthesis; SREBP regulation   |  
| SREBF1 | Up         | Master transcriptional activator    | SREBP regulation; cholesterolbiosynthesis    |  
| CYP51A1| Up         | Sterol 14α-demethylase (P450)       | Cholesterol biosynthesis                     |  
| FASN   | Up         | Fatty acid synthase                 | SREBP activation; lipid metabolism           |  
| TP53   | Up         | Tumor suppressor, transcription     | p53-mediated G2 arrest; apoptosis            |  
| CDC25C | Up         | Phosphatase controlling G2/M entry  | p53-G2 arrest                                |  
| PLK3   | Up         | Polo-like kinase, stress response   | p53-G2 arrest                                |  

*Direction inferred from log2FC > 0 or < 0 in DE results.

Implications  
ISS imposes metabolic and proliferative constraints on CRC cells: by activating SREBP-driven lipid synthesis, cells may buffer membrane and energy homeostasis under low-serum stress, potentially exposing lipid-metabolism enzymes as therapeutic targets. Simultaneous engagement of p53-dependent checkpoints suggests starvation sensitizes cells to DNA-damage signals, offering a rationale to combine ISS with cell-cycle inhibitors.  

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate upregulation of key SREBP targets (HMGCR, FASN) at protein level under ISS.  
2. Test pharmacological inhibition of HMGCR or FASN in combination with ISS to assess synergistic anti-proliferative effects.  
3. Determine whether p53 status modulates the ISS-induced cell-cycle arrest program across CRC genotypes.  
4. Examine Golgi-ER trafficking alterations via imaging to probe nutrient-stress adaptation mechanisms.
